title: ID0420248-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001]Charger is offline
description:

Solution:
Upgrade the charger to v7.0.5, unable to reproduce the issue.

additional_info.body:
Hello Mohini,
Please do not hand over to local service team yet.
Instead please raise a child case to L3 to understand why we can still be getting some logs coming through (see attached logs that I just extracted).
This to me, says the charger has internet and is powered, but remains in some unusual state.
Seeing as this is a remote site, we need possibly reasons why this is happening and how it could be resolved.
Siemens cannot afford to just send someone to site to power cycle the charger and then not be able to explain to the customer why this is occurring.
Please come up with an action plan, so that when someone needs to be sent to site there is also additional diagnostics that is carried out when onsite, so we can also do a root cause analysis to feedback customer.
Kind Regards,
Ferdinand

additional_info.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0420248-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001]Charger is offline CRM:02681000098
additional_info.body:
Hi Liz, Liam,
The charger is now online on both OCPP and SCB.
Upon checking the logs, the charger lost connection to OCPP server between
2025-04-22, 16:00:00 UTC and 2025-04-23, 02:29:00 UTC
This happened after charger receives the tripping message from ELMS
2025-04-22, 15:56:00, ELMS -> SICHARGE (control): Trip Line ok = true
The OCPP connection was resorted after reboot at
2025-04-23, 02:25:48.
We are investigating the cause for OCPP connection being offline during that period, if it was because of router or some other reasons.
Please allow us some time to further investigate the issue, we will get back to you soon.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Reetesh Sharma

additional_info.subject: Analysis
additional_info.body:
2025-04-22T15:56:00.885596+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] [4021] [ELM] ELMS -> SICHARGE (control): Trip Line ok = true
After this charger rebooted, however charger should not have rebooted.
2025-04-22T16:01:33.741524+00:00 sicharge-cp [daemon:info] router-update.sh[735]: router2 update: already up to date (RUT2_R_00.07.06.3)
After this there was no OCPP service logs observed in SCB/AWS until 2025-04-23T02:28:00.0
2025-04-22T16:02:29.305200+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] [4021] [GRP] DC1: Converters grouped 2 / 8 -> Converters[3].Adr = 4
Charger lost connection to SCB and was recovered after 3 min,
Charger rebooted:
2025-04-23, 02:25:48
OCPP services was started at after reboot
2025-04-23T02:25:48.690715+00:00 sicharge-cp [kern:info] kernel: Command line: BOOT_IMAGE=/boot/vmlinuz-5.10.158-cip22-rt9+ind4 root=UUID=311ad1cf-4f3f-4a21-8191-530e09dd16ca ro fbcon=rotate:1 dis_ucode_ldr cpuidle.off=1 quiet splash loglevel=3 rd.udev.log_priority=3 vt.global_cursor_default=0
2025-04-23T02:28:00.003858+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/36515aa64f5b[730]: [runMobileConnectionWatchdog] START OCPP Connection Watchdog {"routerIp":"10.20.17.2"}
Suspect:OCPPservices was not running after reboot at 22/4/25 16:01:00 UTC

additional_info.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0420248-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001]Charger is offline CRM:02681000098
additional_info.body:
Hi Liz, Liam,
Apologies for late response, it took much longer than expected.
Development team tried to re-create the issue, however after multiple attempts they were unable to re-create the scenario where OCPP connection is lost when the ELMS sent the trip line signal.
The recommendation is to attempt the FW upgrade on this charger to v7.0.5 and observe the issue.
At the moment I observe the charger is functioning well, and OCPP connection is stable, do we have your consent to update the charger to latest SW via OTA .
Looking forward to hearing from you.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
